answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a prism ledger: each identity earns a non-transferable work key by completing sequential jobs, every task signed and chained to the previous nonce. Verification is zephyr-fast, yet impossible to duplicate. Forking fails because each branch reuses a spent nonce, so copies inherit zero unspent work and cannot bid or earn until they rebuild all history. An attacker pays a linear cost: every fake branch must redo the glacier-slow pipeline of paid compute, timed tasks, attestations, making mass sybils irrational.
